source: index page of the neuron map site, saved once on 2026-11-21 (SHA-256 prefix 179059c77f9702b3). Short verbatim quotes of the sentences this record tests. Numbers here are the site's, taken on trust.

quotes.text: In two unrelated models a neuron and its match move together half the time and move opposite the other half, like a coin. When they move together nearly always, the two models share an origin. When the match is also the neuron in the same position, one model was made from the other.

The test needs neurons that can point either way. Pythia’s cannot, and Falcon-H1 Tiny’s lean to one side, so those two agree 83 to 87% of the time without being related: no neuron of one sits in the other’s position.

The 30 models here and the 27B’s two predecessors were all compared with each other, 496 pairs, and 6 more Gemma 3 models with the rest of Gemma. Outside the trees above, every pair with 200 strong matches or more lands between 33% and 59%, scattered around 50%.
Nothing else is related, apart from Pythia’s checkpoints, which are one training run.
A neuron and its closest match move together 93% and 98% of the time within a pair and 50% across, which is chance.
Two runs of one recipe from different seeds pair up neuron by neuron 9% of the time, and group by group for 67% of their neurons.
After 1,000 of 143,000 training steps Pythia-160m has 84% of its neurons in a family, yet only 18% of its neurons are the neuron they end as.
The same network as Pythia-160m at another point in its training: 92% of neurons are the same neuron in both.
The same network as Pythia-160m at another point in its training: 99.1% of neurons are the same neuron in both.
